日本利用压电瓷砖将脚步转化为电能。这些瓷砖捕捉来自你脚步的动能。当你行走时，你的重量和动作会对瓷砖产生压力。瓷砖会轻微弯曲，从而产生机械应力。瓷砖内部的压电材料将这种应力转化为电能。每一步都会产生少量电荷，而数百万步结合在一起就能产生足够的电力来驱动 LED 灯、数字显示屏和传感器。在像涩谷车站这样繁忙的地方，每天大约有 240 万个脚步为这一系统作出贡献。这些电能可以被储存或立即使用，从而减少对传统电力来源的依赖，并支持可持续的城市基础设施。这种方法将日常运动转化为实用的可再生能源 #日本 #知识 #事实 #你知道吗 #推荐 #科技 #创新 #历史 #技术 #实验 #热门

Ivy League grade inflation isn’t some mysterious trend. It’s the product of whiny students who think anything below an A is oppression, administrators who refuse to let professors teach, and elite grad programs that quietly reward the fakest transcripts in the country. Students complain, and instead of backing the faculty, administrators rush in to “fix” the situation by pressuring professors to inflate grades. The message is clear: keep the customers happy. Don’t rock the boat. Don’t enforce standards. And hovering in the background are the med schools, law schools, and MBA programs that treat a single B+ like a red flag. Everyone knows these places screen GPA first, so universities respond by padding transcripts to keep acceptance rates high and donors impressed. That’s how you end up with a B+ triggering a formal hearing because “fellowship students only get As.” It’s not rigor. It’s theater. The result? GPAs rise, mastery collapses, and institutions pretend this is what excellence looks like. Ivies better fix this before they lose whatever credibility they have left. - Andreas

As Virginia charged down the field in search of its first touchdown, Luke Mergott forced what should have been a turnover. The redshirt sophomore ripped the ball from J’Mari Taylor and into the hands of teammate Jaiden Francois. But, a facemask penalty on Chandler Rivers snatched the turnover away. On the Cavaliers’ next offensive drive, the Blue Devils stood firm as they forced their opponents to stare down a third-and-2. Then Mergott was called offsides, turning the third-and-2 into a first-and-goal that quickly resulted in Virginia tying the game 7-7. Mergott didn’t let these early mistakes phase him. He simply kept his head up and focused on the next play, providing lockdown coverage that held Virginia to 344 total yards of offense, a far cry compared to the 540 the Cavaliers racked up when the two teams faced off earlier in the season. And, when it mattered most, the 6-foot-3 linebacker came through for his team. After a game-tying touchdown sent the teams to overtime, Duke drew first blood and lined up against the Cavaliers on defense. A roughing-the-passing penalty forced Virginia to start at the 40-yard line instead of the 25. Facing quick pressure, quarterback Chandler Morris scrambled on a trick play and threw the ball to the left side of the field — right into the waiting arms of Mergott. 日本利用压电瓷砖将脚步转化为电能。这些瓷砖捕捉来自你脚步的动能。当你行走时,你的重量和动作会对瓷砖产生压力。瓷砖会轻微弯曲,从而产生机械应力。瓷砖内部的压电材料将这种应力转化为电能。每一步都会产生少量电荷,而数百万步结合在一起就能产生足够的电力来驱动 LED 灯、数字显示屏和传感器。在像涩谷车站这样繁忙的地方, 每天大约有240万个脚步为这一系统作出贡献。这些电能可以被储存或立即使用,从而减少对传统电力来源的依赖,并支持可持续的城市基础设施。这种方法将日常运动转化为实用的可再生能源#日本#知识 #事实 #你知道吗 #推荐 #科技 #创新 #历史 #技术 #实验 #热门

日本利用压电瓷砖将脚步转化为电能。这些瓷砖捕捉来自你脚步的动能。当你行走时，你的重量和动作会对瓷砖产生压力。瓷砖会轻微弯曲，从而产生机械应力。瓷砖内部的压电材料将这种应力转化为电能。每一步都会产生少量电荷，而数百万步结合在一起就能产生足够的电力来驱动LED灯、数字显示屏和传感器。 在像涩谷车站这样繁忙的地方，每天大约有240万个脚步为这一系统作出贡献。这些电能可以被储存或立即使用，从而减少对传统电力来源的依赖，并支持可持续的城市基础设施。这种方法将日常运动转化为实用的可再生能源。 #日本 #知识 #事实 #你知道吗 #推荐 #科技 #创新 #历史 #技术 #实验 #热门

Singapore’s “economic miracle” is the nation's remarkable transformation from a poor, resource‑scarce port in the 1960s to a rich, high‑income global hub within two generations. At independence in 1965, per‑capita income was under US$500 and unemployment was high; by the 2020s it exceeded US$50,000–60,000, making Singapore one of the richest non‑resource economies in the world. This leap came under a strongly interventionist but pro‑market leadership led by Lee Kuan Yew and his technocratic team. The core strategy was export‑oriented industrialisation anchored on foreign investment, not import substitution. Singapore offered political stability, strict anti‑corruption, reliable English‑based law, low and simple taxes, and almost no tariffs, making it the easiest place in the world to do business. The state built world‑class port and airport infrastructure and dedicated industrial estates, then courted multinational manufacturers to produce for global markets rather than the tiny domestic market. At the same time, it invested heavily in mass housing, basic healthcare, and education to create a disciplined, skilled workforce. Over time, Singapore climbed the value chain from labour‑intensive factories into electronics, petrochemicals, logistics, finance, and biomedical research. By liberalising and regulating finance effectively, it became a leading Asian financial centre and foreign‑exchange hub, attracting thousands of multinational regional headquarters. Continuous upgrading of skills and institutions, along with flexible long‑term planning (for example the 1991 Strategic Economic Plan), helped sustain growth even as wages rose and the economy matured. The “miracle” is thus less about luck than about decades of coherent, pragmatic state policy in a very open, globally oriented economy. https://www.emerald.com/insight/content/doi/10.1108/PAP-06-2018-002/full/pdf?title=why-singapore-works-five-secrets-of-singapores-success https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7134611/ https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/0308518X231181128

Logical fallacies are thinking errors that look logical but actually break the rules of reasoning. They often show up in debates, politics, social media, and everyday arguments. Think of them as mental shortcuts that mislead. Some logical fallacies are: 1. Ad Hominem Attacking the person instead of addressing the argument. “You’re stupid, so your point is wrong.” 2. Genetic Fallacy Rejecting a claim because of where it came from, not its truth. “This idea came from TikTok, so it must be false.” 3. Strawman Misrepresenting someone’s argument to make it easier to attack. Original: “We should regulate junk food ads for kids.”� Strawman: “So you want to ban all junk food?” 4. Post Hoc (False Cause) Assuming A caused B just because A happened first. “I wore my lucky t-shirt, and then I topped the test — t-shirt gave me luck!” 5. Slippery Slope Claiming one small step will trigger a chain of disastrous events. “If you skip today’s study session, your whole life will fall apart.” 6. Correlation Fallacy Assuming two things that happen together are related. “People who meditate are rich, meditation causes wealth.” 7. False Dilemma (Either–Or) Presenting only two options when more exist. “Either you’re a topper or you’re a failure.” 8. Equivocation Using one word with two meanings in the same argument. “Theory means guess. Evolution is a ‘theory.’ So evolution is just a guess.” 9. Appeal to Emotion Using feelings instead of reasons. “You should buy this product because it will make your parents proud.” 10. Appeal to Fear Scaring instead of reasoning. “If you don’t believe this, bad things will happen to you.” . . . . . #logicalfallacies #debate #communicationskills

日本利用压电瓷砖将脚步转化为电能。这些瓷砖捕捉来自你脚步的动能。当你行走时，你的重量和动作会对瓷砖产生压力。瓷砖会轻微弯曲，从而产生机械应力。瓷砖内部的压电材料将这种应力转化为电能。每一步都会产生少量电荷，而数百万步结合在一起就能产生足够的电力来驱动LED灯、数字显示屏和传感器。在像涩谷车站这样繁忙的地方，每天大约有240万个脚步为这一系统作出贡献。 这些电能可以被储存或立即使用，从而减少对传统电力来源的依赖，并支持可持续的城市基础设施。这种方法将日常运动转化为实用的可再生能源 ＃日本#知识＃事实#你知道吗#推荐#科技#创新#历史 #技术#验#热门
